title: When Anti-Sycophancy Training Becomes Stubbornness: A Multilingual Study in English, Russian, and Kazakh
description: Research code, frozen configurations, evaluation data, audits, and derived results for matched QLoRA interventions targeting pressure-induced factual answer changes. The v1 intervention produced stubbornness and capability loss; a shared balanced v2 design restored capability, while explicit selective feedback showed no reliable pressure-resistance advantage over the matched control. The release preserves the original translation-confounded Kazakh analysis for provenance and includes a separately versioned corrected Kazakh sensitivity run, which reached the same null conclusion.
